additional_requirements: depressive_episode is present for the majority of the total duration of the active and residual portions of the illness (Criterion C)
delusions_and_hallucinations occur for 2 or more weeks in the absence of a major mood episode (Criterion B)

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.

subtypes.Auditory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of hearing voices or sounds when there is no actual sound.
subtypes.Visual Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of seeing people or objects that do not exist.
subtypes.Tactile Hallucinations: Experiencing the sensation of being touched or movement on the skin when there is no actual stimulus.
subtypes.Olfactory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of smelling odors that do not exist.
subtypes.Gustatory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of tasting flavors that are not actually present.

S022.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
S022.description: A state where behavior and motor control are severely disturbed, appearing as movements or reactions inappropriate to the situation.

subtypes.Childlike Silliness: Inappropriate, childish, or illogical behavior appearing in situations.
subtypes.Stupor: No psychomotor activity; not actively relating to environment.
subtypes.Catalepsy: Passive induction of a posture held against gravity.
subtypes.Waxy Flexibility: Slight, even resistance to positioning by examiner.
subtypes.Mutism: No, or very little, verbal response despite the ability to speak.
subtypes.Negativism: Opposition or no response to instructions or external stimuli without apparent motive.
subtypes.Posturing: Spontaneous and active maintenance of a posture against gravity.
subtypes.Mannerism: Odd, circumstantial caricature of normal actions.
subtypes.Agitation: Excessive motor activity without obvious external cause.
subtypes.Grimacing: Contorted facial expressions irrelevant to the situation.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.

subtypes.Diminished Emotional Expression: A state of reduced emotional expression in facial expressions, eye contact, intonation of speech, and movements.
subtypes.Avolition: A decrease in motivated self-initiated purposeful activities.
subtypes.Alogia: A state where the quantity of spontaneous speech is significantly reduced.
subtypes.Anhedonia: A decrease in the ability to experience pleasure or interest in enjoyable activities.
subtypes.Asociality: A state where interest in social activities or interpersonal relationships is significantly reduced.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.

subtypes.Loss of Interest: Reduced interest in previously enjoyed hobbies or leisure activities.
subtypes.Social Withdrawal: Reduced interest or effort in social interactions and maintaining relationships.
subtypes.Loss of Motivation: Lack of motivation to initiate or complete work or tasks.
subtypes.Anhedonia: Inability to experience positive emotions such as happiness, satisfaction, love, or pleasure.
subtypes.Indifference to Achievement: Insensitivity or indifference to personal achievements or success.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.

subtypes.Significant Weight Loss: Weight loss of more than 5% in a month without dieting.
subtypes.Weight Gain: Weight gain of more than 5% in a month.
subtypes.Decrease in Appetite: Decrease in appetite occurring nearly every day.
subtypes.Increase in Appetite: Increase in appetite occurring nearly every day.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.

subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless repetitive behaviors such as inability to sit still, pacing, hand-wringing, or picking at skin.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Motor): Visible slowing of general body movements, such as walking speed or picking up objects.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Speech): Long response latency or slowed speech when asked a question.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).

subtypes.Feelings of Worthlessness: The feeling that one is useless and has no value.
subtypes.Ruminative Guilt: A thought pattern of obsessively replaying past minor mistakes or flaws and constantly reproaching oneself.
subtypes.Excessive or Inappropriate Guilt: Feeling excessive responsibility for trivial matters or daily events and believing one deserves punishment.
subtypes.Delusional Guilt: Guilt reaching a delusional level, disconnected from reality, involving feeling responsible for unrelated unfortunate events.

symptom.disease_info: Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type) is characterized by a continuous period of illness during which there is a major depressive episode concurrent with symptoms of schizophrenia, such as delusions, hallucinations, or disorganized behavior. Importantly, psychotic symptoms also occur for at least two weeks in the absence of prominent mood symptoms, distinguishing it from mood disorders with psychotic features. The course is often chronic or relapsing, with variable functional impairment in work, relationships, and self‑care, and can range from relatively stable functioning between episodes to marked, enduring disability. Diagnosis requires careful longitudinal assessment to differentiate it from schizophrenia, major depressive disorder with psychotic features, and bipolar spectrum disorders, with attention to the timing and persistence of mood versus psychotic symptoms.

patient.stressor: About three years ago, Johnny’s long‑time warehouse employer underwent a major restructuring, bringing in new automated systems and reducing his hours while pressuring older workers to adapt quickly or consider early retirement. As someone who took pride in his precision and mentorship role, he experienced this shift as a profound threat to his identity and future, and over the following year he became increasingly withdrawn at work, missing safety meetings and turning down chances to train others on the new equipment. Around two years and three months ago, coworkers and his supervisor began noticing that he was having more difficulty concentrating on basic tasks and occasionally stepping away from his forklift mid‑shift, while at home his wife saw him abandon woodworking projects and skip church choir rehearsals. The combination of declining performance reviews, a written warning for safety concerns, and his wife’s alarm at how different he seemed from his usual steady, competitive self led them to contact their primary care physician, who, after ruling out obvious medical causes, referred him to psychiatry when it became clear his functioning had markedly deteriorated.
patient.chief_complaint: “I just don’t care about the things I used to love doing anymore, even my projects in the garage and going out on the river.”

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: I keep thinking the company put some kind of tracking or listening device in the new forklifts and even in my work badge, like they’re watching me specifically and waiting for me to screw up so they can get rid of me, no matter how many times my wife says that’s crazy.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.
S020.manifestation: At work and sometimes even at home in the garage, I hear this man’s voice right behind me saying things like, “You’re dangerous, you’re going to kill someone with that machine,” even when there’s nobody there and no radios on.

S022.name: Disorganized_Abnormal_Behavior
S022.description: A state where behavior and motor control are severely disturbed, appearing as movements or reactions inappropriate to the situation.
S022.manifestation: My wife and coworkers say I’ll just stop the forklift in the middle of the aisle or stand in the kitchen at home staring at the counter for ten, fifteen minutes, kind of frozen, and I don’t even realize how long I’ve been just standing there until someone snaps me out of it.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.
S023.manifestation: Most days I feel like I’m moving and talking through mud, so I barely say two words at the dinner table, can’t show much on my face even when my grandkids are over, and I just sit in my chair instead of helping or joking around like I used to.

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.
S025.manifestation: The weirdest thing is I’ll go out to the garage, look at my half-built fishing boat or the guitars I used to fix up, and I just feel nothing—no excitement, no urge to pick up a tool—so I turn off the light and go back inside.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.
S026.manifestation: I used to pack away big plates after a shift, but now most nights my wife has to remind me to eat because I’m just not hungry and end up pushing the food around, dropping weight without even trying.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.
S027.manifestation: I lie in bed staring at the ceiling for hours, then wake up two or three times a night with my mind racing or hearing that voice, and even on mornings I technically “slept,” I feel like I haven’t really rested at all.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.
S028.manifestation: Some days at the warehouse or even just walking from the living room to the bathroom, my legs feel like they’re made of concrete and I move so slow that people have to wait on me, and it takes me forever to get a sentence out when someone asks a simple question.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).
S030.manifestation: I can’t shake this feeling that I ruined everything—that the layoffs, the safety problems at work, even my wife having to pick up extra shifts are somehow my fault—and I catch myself thinking I don’t deserve to be around my family because all I do is drag them down.
